items.title: Ed Allen Interview, 1961-01-14
items.q: Yeah, I've worked with him. Yeah, well he's gone back to Dixieland.

ctx.x: I know Buckley played a lot of people. I know that they could make a $15, $75 a night just for a fun night. I mean. It's a beer, Billy. But it's not cold. It's not cold. That's all right. I'm not particular about it. I might be good. Yeah. Hey, I'll just let it run out. I'll just let it run out. So Buckley, did you ever work with him on a regular job?
Yeah, I've worked with him. Yeah, well he's gone back to Dixieland. Yeah.

I'll tell you, before, if you're not in the clique you don't get that work. I guess that's in everything. I used to gig what we call club dates and I knew so many people on Friday, Saturday, and I didn't have six, seven jobs. I got a trumpet lady who called me up asking me for a job. They ain't got anything they said? Well I was in that clique they got the work. Well we got the little group that's a tickle crepe. I say where somebody has a job they call me, get me a job from there, of course they ask them how to…
